name: SkilledTradesBC Youth Trades Programs (Discover, Explore, Train and Work in Trades)
org: SkilledTradesBC, with the Ministry of Education and Child Care
city: Across British Columbia (through your high school)
what_you_do: Start a trade while you are still in high school. Train in Trades means trades classes and one level of technical training. Work in Trades means paid on-the-job training while you attend high school.
grades: High school students (grade and age rules are not stated on the pages read)
who_can_apply: Students in high school. The pages read give no grade or age rule. Check the Youth Train in Trades Guide and your school for rules.
pay_detail: Youth Work in Trades training is paid, but no wage is stated. The youth programs page says tuition for these programs is covered. SkilledTradesBC and the Ministry fund technical training done in high school.
duration: From 1 high school course to a year-long program, depending on the program and trade
deadline_text: No application deadline is stated on the pages read. Talk to your school for dates.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school's career educator or work experience coordinator. Train in Trades uses a program guide and a registration form. Work in Trades signs you up as an apprentice with an employer sponsor. It uses a Youth Apprentice and Sponsor Registration Form.
notes: The British Columbia work permit rule for these jobs is not verified. Other ways to find an apprenticeship listed on the site include job boards, WorkBC centres and hiring fairs. Youth Explore the Trades lets you sample several trades.
